result.summary: Reviewed lib/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator.ex (353 lines, new file) directly, independent of ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's summaries. Idiomatic Elixir/OTP: this is correctly a pure function module, not a process -- REQ-030's activate/2 calls it synchronously inside an already-open Repo.transaction/1, so no GenServer/gen_statem is warranted and none was reached for; no supervision concern applies (nothing here needs its own supervised process, so InstanceSupervisor isolation is not at stake). Enum.reduce_while/3 genuinely short-circuits: check_node/3 returns {:cont, :ok} or {:halt, {:error, violation}}, verified by reading the actual reduce_while call site (validate/3, lines 184-188) and check_node's with/else (lines 194-201) rather than trusting the design doc's or ELIXIR-DEV's claim of first-violation-wins -- on the first {:error, violation} the walk stops; it does not accumulate or keep scanning. @enforce_keys is used on both Lookup and Violation (mirrors Graph.Node/Graph.Violation's own convention exactly). @spec/@type coverage is complete on every public function and both nested structs. Pattern-matching style (nested modules, moduledoc source citations with exact .zig line numbers, defp helper chains, string-keyed attribute reads via Map.get with an is_map/1 defensive guard) is consistent with lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex, read in full for comparison -- ref_id/2 is structurally identical in shape and intent to graph.ex's blank_or_missing_string?/2. No unnecessary complexity: build/1 is exactly a one-line closure with no extra logic, matching design doc §4's instruction verbatim. Design-doc conformance, checked directly rather than assumed: Lookup (@enforce_keys [:service_lookup, :plugin_lookup]) and Violation (@enforce_keys [:node_id, :kind, :ref_id, :reason, :message], closed reason() union of exactly the 3 atoms specified) match design doc §3.1/§3.2 exactly; build/1's and validate/3's @spec lines match design doc §4 verbatim, including validate/3 staying public (not defp) for direct testability per the design's own stated reason. Both branch tables re-read clause-by-clause against design doc §5's tables (not re-derived from the design doc's prose, from the actual evaluate_service_lookup/4 and evaluate_plugin_lookup/4 clause heads, lines 246-352): service table's 5 rows (not-registered->violation :service_not_registered, global->pass, tenant+matching-owner->pass, tenant+nil-owner->violation :service_not_available_to_tenant "scope data is inconsistent", tenant+mismatched-owner->violation :service_not_available_to_tenant "is not available to this tenant") match exactly; plugin table's 5 rows (not-registered->PASS [asymmetry 1, INV-SSV-5], global->pass, tenant+matching-owner->pass, tenant+nil-owner->PASS [asymmetry 2, INV-SSV-9, the deliberate inverse of the service table's row 4], tenant+mismatched-owner->violation :plugin_not_available_to_tenant) match exactly, including both R-Co asymmetries preserved as separate, explicit clause heads (never a shared fallthrough that could accidentally couple the two sides). Clause ordering was checked for a subtle correctness question the design doc doesn't explicitly call out: the tenant+matching-owner clause (guard `when owner == tenant_id`) is listed before the tenant+nil-owner clause on both branch tables -- confirmed this ordering cannot mask the nil-owner case, since tenant_id is documented (design doc §4, moduledoc) as always non-nil, so a nil owner can never satisfy `owner == tenant_id` and always falls through to the nil-owner clause correctly regardless of clause order. git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex is independently confirmed empty (ran directly, not trusted from either producer's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's summary) -- this is a purely additive new file; REQ-030 integration is untouched. git diff --stat for the whole branch shows only the new .ex file, its design doc, handoff files, and docs/issues/ISS-0036.yaml -- nothing beyond REQ-031's declared scope was touched, and the Lookup struct-of-functions choice (over a @behaviour) is exactly what the design doc's own §3.1 decided and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already gated; no framework/abstraction machinery appears ahead of what this requirement needs. tenant_id handling checked against docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's 2026-08-17 addendum (population-mechanism decision: tenant_id is derived by the writing context module from the resolved :prefix, never accepted as an independently-trusted caller-supplied field) -- that addendum governs writing a tenant_id column value, which this module never does (it is a pure comparison function with no Repo/write path at all, confirmed by the moduledoc's Purity section and independently by grep). validate/3 receives tenant_id as a plain parameter and only ever compares it via exact equality (owner == tenant_id) against a value returned by an injected lookup -- it does not write, derive, default, or second-guess it in any way, consistent with the design doc's own framing that activate/2 (REQ-030) already derives tenant_id server-side before this hook is reachable (definitions.ex:438, confirmed by direct read). No conflict with Decision 0003 or its addendum. Independently re-ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean, no output/warnings) and mix format --check-formatted (clean) against the current working tree rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's reported results. OQ-1 (REVIEWER opinion, per design doc §9 and SECURITY-REVIEWER's reaffirmation): agree the current generic {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}} fallback is acceptable for now -- a more specific typed error for 'malformed Lookup result' would be a real improvement in a system with a stricter type system (a Rust/OCaml enum return type on the Lookup functions would make this class of bug impossible to construct at all, not just crash-safely at runtime), but building a bespoke typed-error path today would mean designing error handling for a Lookup failure mode that has zero live callers (no real ServiceCatalog/PluginRegistry wiring exists yet, confirmed scope gap) -- that is exactly the kind of ahead-of-need machinery the scope-creep check in this role's charter watches for. Not deferred silently: recommend this be revisited when S3/S6 wire a real Lookup adapter, at which point a malformed-result failure mode becomes reachable from genuine I/O and is worth a typed error. OQ-4 (REVIEWER opinion): agree with the design doc's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's characterization -- the plugin-side nil-owner-passes asymmetry (INV-SSV-9) is a faithful, deliberate port of R-Co's real checkPluginHandler behavior (.zig line 187) and not a bug to fix unilaterally at this requirement's scope, since neither R-Co source states a policy reason to harmonize it with the service side's opposite behavior and REQ-031's acceptance criteria don't ask for that harmonization. Flagging one type-safety observation per this role's charter item 3 (not a blocker): the closed reason()/kind() atom unions here are a reasonable Elixir approximation of a discriminated union, but nothing in Elixir's type system enforces exhaustive matching on them the way an ML-family match statement would -- a future S4 handler pattern-matching on Violation.reason without an exhaustive/else clause could silently miss a new reason atom added later; worth a note for whoever builds that handler, not an action item now.

issues.description: Type-safety gap (REVIEWER charter item 3, noted even though not a blocker): Violation.reason and .kind are closed-set atom unions, which is good practice for this codebase, but Elixir gives no compile-time exhaustiveness check when a future consumer (most likely S4's HTTP 422 renderer) pattern-matches on reason -- a new reason atom added later could silently fall through an non-exhaustive case/cond in that future handler with no compiler warning, unlike a Rust/OCaml match expression which would fail to compile until every variant is handled. No action needed now (no such consumer exists yet); worth flagging to whoever builds the S4 renderer.

Concur with design doc OQ-1 and SECURITY-REVIEWER's reaffirmation: a malformed Lookup return value currently crashes validate/3 with FunctionClauseError, caught generically by activate/2's try/rescue as {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}}. This is fail-closed and acceptable today since no real Lookup implementation is wired into production (explicit scope gap), but a more specific typed error would be a stronger contract once S3/S6 wire a real adapter -- building that now would be speculative error-handling machinery for a failure mode with no live caller, which is itself a form of scope creep this gate watches for, so deferring it is the correct call, not an oversight.
